name: Indian Equatorial Undercurrent - spring reference reach
scope: Declared53 E to91 E spring Indian EUC reference corridor. Longitude gates follow the reviewed 1963 observational domain; OSW chooses the equatorial line, connecting vertices and alternatives. Excludes Wyrtki surface jets, westward undercurrent conventions, anomalous fall episodes and whole-basin endpoints.
layer: Upper-thermocline eastward undercurrent geography. No uniform fixed depth reconstructed; 80.5 E, 50-150 m observations in 1994 are a different local occupation, not this route layer.
time_convention: Spring eastward convention. Review reports several observations between 53 E and 91 E during March-April 1963; those stations do not establish a simultaneous continuous axis or annual recurrence.
source_locator: Schott and McCreary (2001), section3.2.1 printed/PDF29: eastward spring observations at several positions 53-91 E in March-April 1963; displacement and transient structure. Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2 pp29-31 distinguish moorings, years and models. Cited pages reviewed, not source axis digitization.
source_citation: Schott and McCreary (2001), The monsoon circulation of the Indian Ocean, Progress in Oceanography 51, 1-123, doi:10.1016/S0079-6611(01)00083-0.
source_license: Elsevier original retained locally; independent attributed geographic annotations only. No source figures/fields reproduced.
coordinate_selection: Source supports the declared regional geography or study-domain convention. OSW selects all gates, rounded connecting vertices and alternative bends; no velocity axis or source trajectory reconstructed. Independent longitude and endpoint-latitude shifts describe drawing choices, not current width, source position errors or seasonal extrema.

method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 81 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
